purpose: Primary-source material-field evidence batch for Austria student/work and Switzerland third-country work pathways.
policy: Only exact route claims supported by current official sources are included; promotion still requires evidenceIds and complete material-field coverage.

records.claim: Austria's temporary-residence framework includes a residence permit for students; applicants must satisfy the applicable student residence requirements, including admission/enrolment and the general residence conditions that apply to the student category.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian federal immigration temporary-residence guidance and student-specific requirements.

records.claim: For Austrian student residence permits in 2026, the general subsistence reference is EUR 777.58 per month for applicants under 24 and EUR 1,308.39 per month for applicants 24 or older; the required means must cover the applicable period and accommodation costs are considered where relevant.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian federal temporary-residence subsistence requirements for students.

records.claim: Austria's Red-White-Red Card provides residence and employment authorization for qualified third-country workers through defined categories including shortage-occupation workers, other key workers, very highly qualified workers and graduates, subject to category-specific criteria.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian federal permanent-immigration and Red-White-Red Card guidance.

records.claim: Austria's Red-White-Red Card categories have route-specific employment remuneration requirements; for example, the 2026 Other Key Workers category requires statutory minimum remuneration of EUR 3,465 gross per month plus special payments, while other categories use their own salary rules.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian federal Red-White-Red Card category guidance; the numeric claim is explicitly limited to the Other Key Workers sub-route.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking work in Switzerland generally must be highly qualified; the future employer must apply for the permit and demonstrate that no suitable Swiss or EU/EFTA worker is available, subject to the applicable admission rules and quotas.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swiss federal third-country employment-market admission guidance.

records.claim: Swiss third-country employment admission requires salary and employment conditions to comply with the conditions customary to the region, profession and sector; an offered job alone is not sufficient for a work permit.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swiss federal employment-market admission guidance; no unsupported universal salary figure is asserted.
